subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + next steps from our side after the call: 

What we heard:
- Primary requirement: sub-50ms P95 token latency for short responses (average 100-300 tokens) across customer-facing workflows.
- Throughput profile: steady-state ~200 req/s with short bursts up to ~500 req/s (peaks last ~30-90s).
- Data: no on-prem requirement today; data residency in US only.

Our recommendation (short): Based on the latency P95 and bursty throughput, we recommend a Dedicated capacity proof-of-concept (reserved GPU pool) to hit the latency SLO while isolating capacity. Hosted can work for lower-concurrency or non-SLA flows, but Dedicated gives predictable headroom for your peaks.

Attachment: RWI-inference-poc-plan.pdf - high-level PoC plan (benchmarks, required test data, timeline).

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a 24-48h traffic sample (CSV or pcap) and representative prompt set - we can run a benchmark.
2) We schedule a 2-hour benchmarking slot next week (we'll load your traffic shape).
3) If benchmarks look good, we spin up a 30-day Dedicated trial with a baseline reserved config + autoscaling for bursts.

Do you want us to propose an initial config (GPU count / concurrency) or would you like to share the traffic sample first?

Thanks - I'll coordinate with Neha on the PoC runbook.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[attachment: RWI-inference-poc-plan.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finpay.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinPay SRE <sre@finpay.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency & throughput follow-up

Thanks Dylan - helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Our current prod-like tests show ~200 qps average with 10% sustained spikes to ~500 qps during peak morning batch windows; bursts are typically 60-120s.
- Typical prompt length ~300 tokens; some enrichment flows are larger (~1k tokens) but can be routed to async paths.
- Our SLAs: customer-facing chat experiences need P95 < 50ms end-to-end.

We can share a traffic sample. I'll attach a 24-hour sample export (FinPay-traffic-sample.csv).

Two questions up front: 
1) For a Dedicated trial, how do you price the reserved pool vs burst capacity?
2) If we start with Hosted and see latency issues at peaks, can we switch to Dedicated without re-instrumenting the app?

Also cc'ing our SRE to loop them in on the benchmark.

Thanks - Alice
Alice Chen
Head of Product, FinPay
[attachment: FinPay-traffic-sample.csv (CSV, 120KB)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency & throughput follow-up

Dylan - chiming in with technical recommendation and proposed config to include in the reply to Alice: 

Notes:
- With avg prompt ~300 tokens and target P95 < 50ms, we should optimise for GPU-local KV cache and higher token-throughput kernels (quantized where feasible).
- Given 200 qps baseline + 500 qps bursts, initial Dedicated config we recommend for PoC: 4x high-memory inference cards (equivalent to 4x A100-class), configured for continuous batching with a max concurrency per card tuned to your prompt distribution. That config should give ~2-3x the headroom vs. a typical hosted instance and consistent P95s under load.

Fallback/hybrid option:
- Start with Hosted for non-critical/async flows and move critical chat traffic to a Dedicated route. Our routing rules allow per-route policies so you can migrate with no client-side SDK changes - just update the route key.

Pricing & next steps to include in your reply to Alice:
- Offer a 30-day Dedicated PoC at a discounted trial rate (we'll include autoscaling bursts billed at usage rates).
- If PoC is successful, propose a 6-12 month reserved capacity contract for predictable pricing and SLAs.

I'll include the benchmark runbook steps and help schedule the slot after we get the sample.

-Neha
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, FinPay SRE <sre@finpay.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency & throughput follow-up

Alice - thanks for the sample and questions. Short answers + concrete proposal below.

1) Pricing model (trial):
- 30-day Dedicated PoC: discounted reserved baseline for 4x inference GPUs + burst autoscaling. Baseline list price $X/day, trial discount applied - I'll send a formal quote via HubSpot. Burst usage beyond baseline billed at per-GPU-minute usage.

2) Migration path:
- You can start with Hosted for low-SLA workflows and flip critical routes to Dedicated using our routing key. No app re-instrumentation required - just update route config.

Concrete next steps:
- We'll run the benchmark using your attached FinPay-traffic-sample.csv. Neha will define exact benchmarking parameters (latency targets, concurrency shape).
- I'll schedule a 2-hour benchmark slot on Wed 2027-04-07 09:00-11:00 PT - does that work for your SRE?
- I'll follow up with a formal 30-day PoC quote and the trial contract (DocuSign). If you're comfortable, attach a signed NDA and we can start provisioning (I've included our standard NDA link).

Links/attachments included: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FP-2027-041), PoC plan, and a DocuSign contract link to be generated shortly.

If that timeline works I'll put the benchmark on the calendar and loop in our infra team.

Best,
Dylan
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
